test_title: PYST 13: SSC GD Constable - Quantitative Aptitude (Held on: 30th November 2021 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: By selling 90 pens for Rs. 1,557, a shopkeeper loses 30%. How many pens should he sell for Rs. 708 so as to earn a profit of 18%?
solution:
**Given:**

The selling price of 90 pens = Rs. 1557

Loss % = 30%

**Formula used:**

Profit % = (SP - CP)/CP × 100

Loss % = (CP - SP)/CP × 100

**Calculation:**

Selling price (SP) of 90 pens = 1557

Loss % = 30%

∴ Cost Price (CP) of 90 pens = (1557 × 100)/(100 - 30) 

⇒ CP of 90 pens = 15570/7

⇒ CP of 1 pen = 15570/(7 × 90)

⇒ CP of 1 pen = Rs. 173/7

Let P pens be sold to earn a profit of 18%

CP of P pens = 173P/7

SP of P pens = Rs. 708

⇒ Profit % of P pens = (SP of P pens - CP of P pens)/(CP of P pens) × 100

⇒ 18 = (708 - 173P/7)/(173P/7) × 100

⇒ 18 = (708 × 7/173P - 1) × 100

⇒ 118 = 708 × 7 × 100/173P

⇒ P = (708 × 7 × 100)/(173 × 118)

⇒ P = 24.27

∵ The number of Pens cannot be in decimal, we take the value of P as the nearest integer i.e. P = 24

**∴ 24 Pens should be sold for Rs. 708 so as to earn a profit of 18%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Formula used:**

Let N1 = initial number of items, P1 % or L1 % = initial Profit % or Loss %, SP1 = initial Selling Price

And, N2 = final number of items, P2 % or L2 % = final Profit % or Loss %, SP2 = final Selling price

Then the relation between the two is given by

In case of Profit % is given

⇒ [N1 × (100 + P1 %)]/SP1 = [N2 × (100 + P2 %)]/SP2 

If Loss % is given

⇒ [N1 × (100 - L1 %)]/SP1 = [N2 × (100 - L2 %)]/SP2

**Calculation:**

N1 = 90, L1 = 30%, SP1 = Rs. 1557

N2 = P (Let), P2 = 18%, SP2 = 708

⇒ (90 × 70)/1557 = (P × 118)/708

⇒ P = 24.27 

∴ 24 pens should be sold
